item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports intervention-based history attribution, but the retrieved literature does not establish the exact fixed-suffix, matched-context GRU probe proposed here. [Demystifying Sequential Recommendations (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal discrete history changes that alter recommendations. [CoDeR (2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379) and [CoDeR+ (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3778863) address demand shifts and confounding; they motivate separating drift from noise but do not establish that observed ranking changes reveal user intent. Earlier [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073) supplies recurrent-model event attribution and temporal pruning, useful as a reference diagnostic.\n\nA [September 2026 temporal-attribution benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201) reports strong faithfulness and robustness for Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP, while raw attention performs poorly; its evaluated backbones exclude GRUs, so transfer requires verification. The [2024 faithfulness survey](https://aclanthology.org/2024.cl-2.6/) also highlights distribution-shift problems with erasure. Together, these findings motivate a proposed paired probe: preserve latest suffix, target, candidates, event count and padding; replace older items using training-history matches on popularity, timestamp and available title/description similarity; separately shuffle the older prefix to isolate order dependence. Measure paired target-margin, rank and HR@10 changes across replacement draws, comparing them with embedding Integrated Gradients and recorded GRU gates. Include unchanged-input controls and uncertainty intervals. Treat gate/gradient agreement as supporting evidence of model sensitivity; useful memory requires improved target ranking, distractor sensitivity requires harmful influence, and neither establishes actual preference drift or intent."}
